newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian GIMV IPO oversubscribed four times.
newsitem.headline: Belgian GIMV IPO oversubscribed four times.

text.p: The initial public offering of shares of GIMV, the investment company of the Belgian regional government of Flanders, has been oversubscribed four times, brokerage Petercam said on Friday.

To accommodate demand from retail investors, institutional investors' share of the issue was cut to 45 percent from 60 percent. Even after this re-allocation, demand from private investors still exceeded the offer size three times, Petercam said.

Two-thirds of the shares allocated for private investors would be given to those who ordered via Kredietbank, its KB-Securities, its Bank van Roeselare, and HSA-Spaarkrediet, ASLK, NMKN and Bank Degroof. Petercam said on Thursday that subscriptions for the GIMV IPO were closed five days ahead of schedule.
The offer, a combined private placement for institutional investors and an initial public offer aimed at private investors, involves a maximum 4,599,770 shares, or 19.9 percent of GIMV's capital.
Trading in the shares, priced at 2,010 francs each, starts on June 26.
GIMV invests in unlisted Flemish growth companies, often bringing them to the bourse when they reach maturity.
It main interest is 33.99 percent of Belgian electronics firm Barco. It also has 9.99 percent of Belgian engineering company BMT and a small interest in Nasdaq-listed Belgian software firm Xeikon.

It is a shareholder in Europe's Easdaq growth stocks market and in Belgian telecommunications group Telenet, which aims to convert Flanders' cable television network to provide multimedia and voice telephone services from 1998.
